name: Curve/Vyper reentrancy exploit and CRV contagion scare (July 30 – August 2023)
speed: ~$70M drained across 4 pools within ~6-7 hours on Jul 30; Curve TVL -47% in ~2 days; CRV ~-34% peak-to-trough in ~2 days (instantaneous ~-88% print on DEX during the drain); the systemic (Egorov liquidation) overhang played out over ~1 week
summary: 30 июля 2023: reentrancy-баг компилятора Vyper 0.2.15-0.3.0 — ~$70M выкачано из пулов Curve, TVL Curve −47% за 2 дня, CRV −34% (на DEX печатал $0.086). Системная угроза второго порядка: CRV-займы Egorov ~$100M+ на Aave/Frax/Abracadabra — ликвидация в неликвидный CRV дала бы bad debt Aave; разряжено OTC-продажами. Для книги — задокументированный near-miss канала «bad debt социализируется на USDC-саплаеров» + Fraxlend с utilization 100% на дни. Книга SPA на 2026-08: aave_v3 40% / pendle (PT_USDC) 20% / maple 15% / morpho_steakhouse 15% / кэш USDC 10%.

timeline.event: Vyper compiler v0.2.15 ships a change to set_storage_slots that mis-allocates the storage slots backing @nonreentrant locks: different functions sharing a named lock get DIFFERENT slots, silently disabling cross-function reentrancy protection. Bug persists through v0.2.16 and v0.3.0; fixed in v0.3.1 (late 2021) but already-deployed pools compiled with vulnerable versions remain live.

Pre-history of the second-order risk: Gauntlet proposes freezing CRV and setting CRV LTV to 0 on Aave v2 Ethereum, citing Egorov's ~$67.7M USDT/USDC debt against ~$185M CRV collateral; Aave community votes the proposal down (~June 18).

First exploit transaction targets JPEG'd's pETH/ETH Curve pool; the exploiter is front-run by an MEV searcher who drains 6,106.65 WETH (~$11.4M) using the same reentrancy technique (add_liquidity/remove_liquidity cross-function reentrancy through raw ETH calls).

Metronome msETH/ETH pool drained: 866.55 WETH (~$1.6M) + 959.71 msETH (~$1.8M). In parallel (14:49 UTC) Curve alerts Alchemix; Alchemix multisig starts pulling liquidity at 14:55 UTC but the alETH/ETH pool is drained of 7,258.70 WETH (~$13.6M) + 4,821.55 alETH (~$9M).

CRV/ETH pool drained (~$24.7M: 7,193,401.77 CRV + 7,680.49 WETH + 2,879.65 ETH). CRV's deepest on-chain liquidity venue is destroyed; CRV prints as low as ~$0.086 on DEXes. White-hat MEV bot c0ffeebabe.eth front-runs part of the attack, capturing the 2,879.65 ETH (~$5.4M). (Exact hour approximate; evening UTC per postmortems.)

Chainlink's CRV/USD feed, aggregating CEX prices, floors around $0.59 while DEX spot collapses — Aave and other lenders see no liquidation-triggering price, averting a cascade off the manipulated on-chain print.

July 30 becomes the most profitable MEV day in Ethereum history: ~6,006 ETH (~$11M) in MEV rewards, including a record single-block reward of 584.05 ETH (> $1M) from front-running exploit transactions. Copycat attacks on BNB Chain (Ellipsis ~$68.6k) and deBridge (~$24.6k); Arbitrum Tricrypto pool flagged as potentially vulnerable, LPs told to exit as precaution (not exploited).

Panic withdrawals: Curve TVL collapses from $3.26B (Jul 30) toward $1.73B by Aug 1 (-47%, DeFiLlama). CRV falls ~20-30% on CEXes. Focus shifts to the SECOND-ORDER threat: Egorov's CRV-collateralized stablecoin loans — 63.2M USDT on Aave v2 (against ~$168M / 288M+ CRV, >30% of circulating supply, liquidation price ~0.3767 CRV/USDT), 15.8M FRAX on Fraxlend (59M CRV), 18.76M MIM on Abracadabra — ~97.76M stables against ~427.5M CRV (~47% of circulating supply), plus a DOLA line on Inverse Finance.

c0ffeebabe.eth returns the 2,879 ETH (~$5.4M) to the Curve deployer, and later ~955 msETH/$1.6M to Metronome. Fraxlend emerges as the most acute fuse: its Time-Weighted Variable Interest Rate doubles every 12h at 100% utilization (path to ~10,000% APY in ~3.5 days), threatening to liquidate Egorov regardless of CRV price; Egorov deploys an incentivized Curve pool to pull FRAX liquidity in and pays Fraxlend down first.

CRV hits a seven-month low around $0.48 on CEXes. Egorov begins OTC sales at ~$0.40/CRV with informal lockups: Justin Sun (~5M CRV), Machi Big Brother (3.75M), DWF Labs (2.5M), Cream Finance, DCFGod and others — ultimately 106M CRV for ~$46M in early August (one later accounting: cumulative ~158.65M CRV to 53 buyers for ~$63.46M across August).

Egorov has raised ~$42.4M and paid down debt but still owes ~$80M on-chain. crvUSD briefly depegs by ~0.35% before PegKeepers restore it. Curve, Metronome and Alchemix jointly offer the attacker a 10% bounty / no legal action if 90% is returned by August 6.

Returns begin: JPEG'd receives back 5,494.4 WETH (attacker keeps 610.6 WETH as the 10% bounty); on Aug 4-5 the alETH exploiter returns all 4,820.55 alETH + WETH to Alchemix ('I'm refunding you... because I don't want to ruin your project').
Bounty deadline passes with the CRV/ETH exploiter not returning the remainder; Curve opens the $1.85M bounty to the public for identifying the attacker.
Curve announces ~73% of hacked funds ($52.3M of ~$70M+) recovered; acute phase over. Liquidation threat is defused via OTC paydowns; no bad debt realized on Aave.

Aave DAO response: Chaos Labs proposals (votes ended Aug 12) disable CRV borrowing on Aave v3 Ethereum and Polygon and reduce the CRV liquidation threshold on v2; Gauntlet's renewed proposal to freeze the CRV reserve on Aave v2 Ethereum (freezeReserve, ARFC dated Aug 19) follows — CRV can no longer back new borrowing on v2.
Egorov deposits ~$35M more CRV and fully settles his Aave debt position, closing the largest single systemic exposure; remaining debt across other venues cut to ~$42.7M.

Curve DAO vote (~94% yes) approves ~$49.2M reimbursement to LPs of the affected pools (alETH/ETH, pETH/ETH, msETH/ETH, CRV/ETH): ~$7.2M of white-hat-recovered ETH plus ~$42M in CRV covering unrecovered losses and missed emissions — LPs effectively made whole.

crv.window: 2023-07-30 -> 2023-08-01 (CEX prices; sources report the initial leg variously as -19% to $0.59, -25% to $0.548, and the Aug 1 seven-month low of ~$0.48; on-chain DEX prints touched ~$0.086 during the CRV/ETH pool drain but were never the oracle price)

btc.window: 2023-07-30 -> 2023-08-07; BTC ~$29k range, essentially unaffected — the event was idiosyncratic to Curve/CRV; no sourced BTC drawdown attributable to it

eth.window: 2023-07-30 -> 2023-08-07; ETH dipped only modestly (~$1.85-1.88k range); no sourced event-attributable drawdown

aleth_peth_mseth.window: LST-pegged assets alETH/pETH/msETH lost their primary liquidity venue and traded at discounts to ETH after the drains; magnitudes not reliably sourced (null). Curve killed gauges on affected pools and spun up new plain pools

crvusd.window: 2023-08-03 brief depeg (~0.35% below $1), PegKeeper restored peg same day

stablecoins.notes: Brief wobble on post-hack uncertainty; PegKeeper algorithm restored peg within the day. Curve's crvUSD stable pools were named among exploited pools in some reports but crvUSD itself stayed effectively pegged.
No depeg — this event did not stress fiat-backed stablecoin pegs.
No depeg; USDT was the asset Egorov had borrowed on Aave — utilization/borrow-rate pressure, not peg pressure.

LST/synthetic-ETH pegged assets lost their primary liquidity venue when the pools were drained and traded at discounts to ETH; exact discount magnitudes not reliably sourced (null). Included because peg behavior of pool-quoted synthetics is the direct analog for PT/vault share pricing.
Lender-side stress (Abracadabra raised rates; Fraxlend utilization hit 100% with rate-doubling ramp; Inverse capped exposure) rather than peg breaks.

tvl.window: 2023-07-30 -> 2023-08-01 (DeFiLlama); one intraday snapshot showed -42% to $1.87B on Jul 31; Curve TVL remained depressed for months (2-year lows later in 2023)

recoveries_usd.notable: c0ffeebabe.eth returned 2,879 ETH ($5.4M) + ~$1.6M msETH; JPEG'd got 5,494.4 WETH back (610.6 WETH kept as 10% bounty); Alchemix got all 4,820.55 alETH + WETH back; Curve DAO approved $49.2M LP reimbursement Dec 21 2023 (94% yes)

bad_debt_usd.narrowly_avoided: Liquidation of Egorov's Aave v2 position (63.2M USDT against 288M+ CRV = >30% of circulating supply, liq price ~$0.3767 vs CRV low ~$0.48) would have dumped collateral into a market whose main on-chain venue had just been drained — widely assessed as certain to leave large Aave v2 bad debt requiring the Safety Module (AAVE-token) backstop; no precise consensus dollar estimate, so left unquantified

defi_impact.gas_mev: Jul 30 was the most profitable MEV day in Ethereum history: ~6,006 ETH (~$11M) in MEV rewards incl. a record 584.05 ETH single-block reward; gas spiked during the exploit window as bots fought to front-run
defi_impact.oracles: Decisive factor: Chainlink CRV/USD (CEX-price aggregation) floored ~$0.59 while DEX spot printed ~$0.086 — lending protocols never saw the manipulated price, so no false-liquidation cascade. Flip side: protocols relying on DEX/spot oracles would have liquidated into nothing. Curve pools' internal price oracles were the manipulated object itself.
defi_impact.withdrawal_freezes: No user withdrawal freezes on Curve's unaffected pools; affected-pool LPs lost funds instantly rather than being frozen. Post-crisis, Aave FROZE the CRV reserve on v2 (no new CRV-backed borrowing) and disabled CRV borrowing on v3 Ethereum/Polygon (votes ended Aug 12); Fraxlend hit 100% utilization (lenders temporarily could not withdraw FRAX until Egorov repaid).
defi_impact.protocols_paused_or_insolvent: None insolvent. JPEG'd/Alchemix/Metronome paused/removed Curve liquidity; Curve killed gauges on affected pools and deployed replacement pools; Arbitrum Tricrypto LPs advised to exit as precaution.
defi_impact.bridges_chains: No chain halts. Copycat exploits on BNB Chain (Ellipsis, ~$68.6k) and deBridge (~$24.6k); Vyper-compiled contracts across chains had to be triaged.

causes.primary: Latent Vyper compiler bug (v0.2.15/0.2.16/0.3.0): @nonreentrant lock storage slots mis-allocated by set_storage_slots, so named reentrancy locks did not actually guard across functions — enabling cross-function reentrancy on Curve pools with raw-ETH callbacks that were compiled with those versions.
secondary: Compiler-level vulnerability class: audits of the pool contracts could not see it; the vulnerable versions were ~2 years old and which deployed contracts used them was not tracked anywhere.

Concentration of a single founder's leverage: ~$100M of stablecoin debt across Aave v2/Fraxlend/Abracadabra/Inverse against ~47% of CRV circulating supply, with Aave v2 lacking supply caps/isolation to prevent it.
Reflexivity: the exploit drained the CRV/ETH pool that WAS the main on-chain CRV liquidity, so the same event that cut CRV's price also removed the exit liquidity a liquidation would have needed.
Fraxlend's time-weighted rate mechanism at 100% utilization created a second, price-independent liquidation fuse (rates doubling every 12h toward ~10,000% APY).
causes.mechanism: Vyper compiler mis-compiles reentrancy locks -> attacker (and front-running MEV bots) reenter add_liquidity/remove_liquidity on 4 Curve ETH-paired pools on Jul 30, draining ~$70M -> CRV crashes ~30% (CEX) / ~$0.086 (DEX) and Curve TVL halves on panic withdrawals -> Egorov's CRV-collateralized loans approach liquidation (Aave liq px ~$0.3767 vs CRV ~$0.48) -> feared forced sale of 300M+ CRV into a market whose main on-chain venue was just drained -> projected Aave v2 bad debt and Safety Module (AAVE token) backstop event -> defused by: Chainlink CEX-priced oracle floor blocking manipulated-price liquidations, Egorov's OTC sales (~106M CRV @ ~$0.40) and debt paydowns, white-hat/hacker returns (73% of funds), and Aave governance freezing/disabling CRV markets.

contagion: Vyper compiler bug (broken reentrancy locks in 0.2.15/0.2.16/0.3.0) -> 4 Curve ETH-paired pools drained ~$70M (pETH/ETH ~$11.4M, msETH/ETH ~$3.4M, alETH/ETH ~$22.6M, CRV/ETH ~$24.7M) + BNB-chain copycats (~$73k) + deBridge (~$24.6k)
CRV/ETH pool drain destroys CRV's deepest on-chain liquidity; DEX CRV prints ~$0.086; CRV -20-30% on CEXes to ~$0.48
Curve TVL -47% in ~2 days ($3.26B -> $1.73B) on panic withdrawals; alETH/pETH/msETH depeg vs ETH; crvUSD briefly -0.35%

CRV crash puts Egorov's ~$100M CRV-backed loans (Aave v2 63.2M USDT; Fraxlend 15.8M FRAX with rate-doubling fuse; Abracadabra 18.76M MIM; Inverse DOLA) within ~25% of liquidation (Aave liq px ~$0.3767)

Feared liquidation of 30%+ of CRV circulating supply into a market with no depth -> projected Aave v2 bad debt -> Aave Safety Module / AAVE-token selloff scenario -> DeFi-wide confidence shock (traders piled into CRV shorts; lenders Aave/Abracadabra/Inverse rushed parameter changes)

Defused before impact: Chainlink CEX-priced feed floored ~$0.59 (no false liquidation trigger); Egorov OTC-sold ~106M CRV @ ~$0.40 to Justin Sun/DWF/Machi/others and repaid Fraxlend then Aave; hacker + white-hats returned 73% of funds by Aug 7; Aave froze CRV on v2 and disabled CRV borrowing on v3

recovery.recovered: mostly — LPs made whole, but protocol metrics did not mean-revert
recovery.time_to_recover: Funds: 73% returned within 8 days; LPs fully compensated ~5 months later (Dec 21 2023 vote). Systemic threat: defused within ~1 week (OTC sales + paydowns); Aave exposure fully closed Sept 27 2023. Markets: CRV never regained its pre-hack $0.73 level in 2023 and Curve TVL stayed at roughly half its pre-hack level for months (2-year lows into late 2023).
recovery.notes: Recovery was discretionary, not mechanical: it depended on the attacker accepting a 10% bounty, white-hat MEV bots choosing to return funds, 50+ whales buying OTC at $0.40 with handshake lockups, and a DAO voting treasury CRV to victims. None of these channels can be assumed in a stress model. The same Egorov overhang re-emerged in June 2024, when CRV fell ~30% and his positions WERE liquidated (~$140M CRV) — evidence that the 2023 defusal deferred rather than eliminated the risk.

confidence_notes: Observed facts, well-multi-sourced: Vyper versions 0.2.15/0.2.16/0.3.0 and root cause (official Vyper post-mortem); per-pool token amounts (LlamaRisk postmortem); Curve TVL $3.26B->$1.73B (DeFiLlama via CryptoSlate); 73%/$52.3M recovered by Aug 7; JPEG'd 5,494.4 WETH return with 610.6 WETH bounty; Alchemix 4,820.55 alETH return; c0ffeebabe 2,879 ETH; Aave votes (June rejection, Aug 10-12 proposals); Dec 21 2023 $49.2M reimbursement; Egorov settling Aave in Sept 2023. CONTESTED/APPROXIMATE: (1) total loss ranges $61M-$73.5M across sources depending on whether white-hat front-run funds, BSC/deBridge copycats, and CRV-at-what-price are counted — '~$70M' is the standard headline; (2) CRV price path: pre-exploit $0.73-0.75, first-leg drop reported variously -19%/-25%, Aug 1 low ~$0.48 (some cite $0.481); the $0.086 was a DEX-only print, and the '$0.59 Chainlink floor' comes from one analytics writeup (medium confidence); (3) Egorov debt totals moved daily: Delphi's Aug-1 snapshot 97.76M stables vs 427.5M CRV (47% of supply) vs Gauntlet's June $67.7M/$185M vs press '$100M+/~$110M' — the brief's 'Aave ~$63M' is CONFIRMED (63.2M USDT); Inverse Finance's ~10M DOLA figure is a September snapshot, his July 30 Inverse exposure is not precisely sourced (partly why totals differ); (4) OTC totals: 106M CRV/~$46M is the widely cited early-August figure; one retrospective counts 158.65M CRV/~$63.46M to 53 buyers across all of August — both reported; (5) intraday times 13:10/14:17/14:49-14:55/14:50 UTC are from postmortems (high confidence); the CRV/ETH drain 'evening UTC' hour is inferred (marked observed=false); (6) potential Aave bad-debt size had liquidation fired was never authoritatively quantified — left null rather than invented; (7) the brief's 'TVL -47%' and 'CRV -30%+' are CONFIRMED; its 'Egorov $100M+' is confirmed as order-of-magnitude with the per-protocol split above. INFERENCE (labeled as such): all SPA mapping content, and the Blockworks mention of a 'Pendle pETH-ETH pool' among victims appears to be a misattribution of JPEG'd's pETH — no other source corroborates Pendle losses, so none are claimed.

data_availability.price_series: FREE: Binance public market-data (data.binance.vision) 1m/1h/1d klines for CRVUSDT, ETHUSDT, BTCUSDT, FRAXUSDT covering Jul-Aug 2023 — best granularity for CRV's crash and recovery; OKX/Bybit similar. CoinGecko free API gives daily (and hourly for recent windows only) — 2023 history at daily granularity is free via /market_chart/range for top coins; CryptoCompare free hourly. NOT free: the on-chain DEX print (~$0.086) — needs archive-node pool-state replay or GeckoTerminal/Kaiko paid history; treat as a documented spike, not a replayable series.
data_availability.stablecoin_prices: FREE: DeFiLlama stablecoins API (daily prices/pegs) covers crvUSD, USDC, USDT, FRAX, MIM, DOLA for the window. alETH/pETH/msETH vs ETH discounts: CoinGecko has alETH daily (patchy); pETH/msETH coverage is poor — mark ETH-pegged synthetic discounts as approximate or reconstruct from Curve pool swap events (needs archive node / free Dune queries).
data_availability.tvl: FREE and good: DeFiLlama API daily TVL for curve-dex (shows $3.26B->$1.73B), aave-v2, aave-v3, alchemix, jpegd, metronome, fraxlend, abracadabra; per-pool Curve TVL series also on DeFiLlama /pool endpoints (yields dataset) at daily granularity.
data_availability.liquidations: PARTIAL/FREE-WITH-EFFORT: no free one-call aggregate. Aave v2/v3 LiquidationCall events via the free Aave subgraph or Dune free tier reconstruct per-market liquidations (this event's point: ~zero CRV liquidations executed — the crisis is in the counterfactual). CEX futures liquidations for CRV: Coinglass shows recent data free but historical export is paid — mark paid.
data_availability.gas: FREE: Etherscan API (free key) daily average gas price; Dune free tier for intraday Jul 30 gas/priority-fee spikes; MEV data free via mevboost.pics and Flashbots public relay datasets (the 584 ETH block is block-level public data).
data_availability.defi_rates: FREE: DeFiLlama yields API has historical APY snapshots for Aave USDC/USDT and Curve pools at daily granularity — captures the borrow-rate/utilization spike channel. Fraxlend historical utilization/rates: reconstructable from contract events (free RPC + effort), not from any free API.
data_availability.not_obtainable_free: Intraday order-book depth / CEX-DEX liquidity depth (Kaiko paid — key for modeling 'liquidation into thin liquidity'); tick-level Curve pool reserve history without an archive node; Chainlink round-by-round historical answers are technically free (feed contract logs via public RPC) but high-effort; OTC transaction terms (off-chain, only press-reported).

positions_hit.aave_v3_usdc: Most directly analogous exposure. The 2023 crisis was on Aave v2, but the mechanism transfers: as a USDC supplier, the portfolio is short protocol bad-debt — a whale's collateral (CRV then; any long-tail collateral now) liquidating into thin on-chain liquidity socializes losses onto suppliers. Secondary channel: stress makes utilization spike (borrowers top up / lenders flee), so supply APY jumps AND withdrawals can temporarily fail at ~100% utilization — exactly what FRAX lenders on Fraxlend experienced for days.
positions_hit.morpho_steakhouse_usdc: Morpho Blue vaults did not exist in July 2023 (no historical series to replay directly). Mapped risk: curated vault allocates USDC into isolated markets whose collateral can be a CRV-like token; a compiler-class exploit or collateral-liquidity collapse in one market hits the vault share price with zero advance APY signal. Oracle choice (CEX-anchored Chainlink vs DEX spot) determines whether the market liquidates correctly, too early, or into nothing.
positions_hit.pendle_pt: Pendle was not materially hit in 2023 (the drained 'pETH' was JPEG'd's, not Pendle's, despite some confused reporting). Mapped risk: PT trades on AMM pools compiled/audited code paths just like Curve's; an exploit or panic drains PT/underlying AMM liquidity, gapping PT mark-to-market far below fair value. Hold-to-maturity recovers face value ONLY if the underlying yield source (e.g., an Aave/Morpho market) itself stays solvent — the two failure modes correlate in a Curve-style event.
positions_hit.maple: Least affected channel in this event (credit/RWA venue, USDC intact). Indirect: risk-off after the exploit widened DeFi credit spreads and TVL flight; a Maple-style venue's lockups mean the portfolio cannot de-risk mid-event.
positions_hit.cash_10pct: USDC held peg throughout — the 10% cash buffer was genuinely safe in this scenario, and was the only sleeve that could have funded opportunistic rebalancing (CRV at $0.40 OTC was the trade of the month for whales).

TVL floors and live-TVL checks (SPA's ADR-053) do not capture COLLATERAL-side concentration (one address = 30%+ of a collateral's supply).

Exploit tail: a compiler-level bug bypasses audit-based whitelisting entirely — Curve was the most battle-tested DeFi protocol; whitelist status is not a stochastic APY haircut but a jump-to-loss process (~-100% on affected pool principal, with recovery a slow, discretionary variable: 73% in a week here, then DAO reimbursement 5 months later).

Oracle-regime assumption: USDC=1 was fine here, but CRV-at-Chainlink vs CRV-on-DEX diverged 7x for hours. Any liquidation/kill-switch logic reading on-chain spot would have fired massively wrong; SPA's fail-CLOSED refusal on feed divergence is exactly the correct behavior this event validates.

Contagion latency: the systemic phase (Egorov loans) took DAYS and was defused by off-chain OTC deals invisible to on-chain data — a daily-cycle system would see peg=1, TVL falling, APY spiking, and would need the drawdown ladder (SOFT -5%/HARD -10%) plus per-protocol freeze rather than any single-metric trigger.
